title: Joystick Snake
intro: Steer a snake around an 8×8 LED matrix with a joystick. Eat the dots to grow!

steps.title: Read the joystick
steps.text:
A joystick is two potentiometers (left-right and up-down) plus a button you press by pushing it down.

**Your task:** Run, open the **Serial Monitor**, and move the joystick around.
hints: In the middle, both numbers are about half of the biggest number.
In the simulator, drag the joystick's knob.
Push the joystick down to see "pressed: yes".

checks.label: The numbers change as I move the joystick

steps.success: Two analog inputs and a button in one part!

steps.title: A dot on the matrix
steps.text:
The LED matrix is a grid of 8 × 8 lights. Rows and columns are numbered 0 to 7. `matrix.setPoint(row, column, true)` turns one on.

**Your task:** move the dot to the bottom-right corner, then Run.
hints: The last row and column are number 7.
The bottom-right corner is row 7, column 7.

checks.label: The dot is in the corner
I can see the dot in the corner

steps.success: Every picture on a screen is just dots like this: lots of them.

steps.title: Move the dot
steps.text:
Now steer the dot. `x` is the column and `y` is the row. Push the joystick past a quarter of the way and the dot moves one step, but never off the edge.

**Your task:** fill in the blanks so the dot moves right and down too.
hints: Left takes 1 away from x (`x--`). Right is the opposite.
steps.success: You're steering! That's the start of every video game.

steps.title: Snake
steps.text: **Goal:** the snake game. A snake of 3 dots moves by itself; the joystick steers. Eating the food dot makes it 1 longer and puts new food somewhere random. Hitting the edge or itself is game over: print `Game over!` and start again.
hints: Keep the snake in two arrays, `snakeX` and `snakeY`; part 0 is the head.
To move, shift every part one place back (from the tail end), then put the new head at the front.
Use **Watch the goal**, then build it one piece at a time: move, steer, food, crash.

checks.label: The snake is stored in arrays

steps.success: You made Snake! It was one of the first games on mobile phones.

outro: Snake! You used **arrays** to remember every part of the snake, **coordinates** to place dots on a grid, and a game loop that reads input, updates and draws.
stretch: Speed the snake up as it grows.
Show the score as a number in the Serial Monitor when the game ends.
Let the snake wrap around the edges instead of crashing.
